hints.en: `sort_values("score", ascending=False)` gives a **new table** sorted largest first.

hints.en: `.head(3)` for the first three rows; `[["name", "score"]]` for two columns.

hints.tr: `idxmax()` en büyüğün **satır etiketini** veriyor; onu `data.loc[etiket, "name"]` içinde kullanabilirsin.
hints.en: `idxmax()` gives the **row label** of the largest; you can use it in `data.loc[label, "name"]`.

hints.tr:
Çözüm:

```python
ranked = data.sort_values("score", ascending=False)

print(ranked[["name", "score"]].head(3))
print(data.loc[data["score"].idxmax(), "name"])
print(list(ranked.index))
```
hints.en:
The solution:

```python
ranked = data.sort_values("score", ascending=False)

print(ranked[["name", "score"]].head(3))
print(data.loc[data["score"].idxmax(), "name"])
print(list(ranked.index))
```
